UNIT TYPE SCHEDULE 26/09/2024

Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

No works shall take place following completion of the ground floor slab level, until a schedule of all materials to be used in the external elevations, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be  carried out other than in accordance with the approved materials and details. 

Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

Prior to first occupation of the development, the 5 residential parking bay identified on drawing Proposed Ground Floor Plan Site A (0824-BPA-SA-00-DR-A-P1100 C) and 12 residential parking bays identified on drawing Proposed Ground Floor Plan Site B (0824-BPA-SB-00-DR-A-P1110B) shall be provided on site. The spaces shall only be used for the parking of private motor vehicles and shall not be used for any other purpose.  
 
Reason: To ensure the development provides adequate on site car parking

Following the practical completion of the development, an updated Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, reflecting the measures taken in practice in Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the Energy hierarchy to reduce carbon emitted from the operation of a development and its services, as committed to in the design stage, and the amended New Development Carbon Compensation to be paid for the remaining emissions. 

Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets by renewable energy are met .

The approved overheating strategy shall be implemented prior to first occupation and maintained on site, including: 

a. Utilizing glazing with a G value of 0.37 (BS EN 410) or less 
b. Incorporating KERS Cool Boost system (or equivalent to provide cooled tempered air to apartments). Boosted cooling ventilation to provide a minimum of 50 l/s of cooled tempered air from each KERS unit to serve all habitable rooms in all apartments/houses. 
c. Opening tilt and turn windows with a number of windows fitted with a turn restrictor with a 250mm or 300mm cable to allow increased ventilation. 

Reason: To ensure that suitable living conditions are achieved within the development and that the buildings do not overheat

The residential unit(s) hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the Building Regulations Optional requirement G2 for water consumption of no more than 105 litres or less per head per day (excluding allowance of up to five litres for external water consumption) has been complied with. The measures shall thereafter be permanently retained.

Reason: The site is in an area of water stress requiring water efficiency opportunities to be maximised to mitigate the impacts of climate change and enhance the sustainability of the development.

The residential unit(s) hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the play areas have been fully provided on site in accordance with the approved plans and made available for use. These facilities shall thereafter be retained and maintained for their intended purpose for the lifetime of the development.

Reason: To ensure that adequate play space is provided for the recreational needs of children living within the development, in the interests of promoting healthy lifestyles and creating a child-friendly environment

The residential unit(s) hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the development has been carried out in full accordance with the submitted Fire Statements. The approved fire safety measures shall be implemented prior to occupation and thereafter maintained for the lifetime of the development.

Reason: To ensure that appropriate fire safety measures are incorporated into the development

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until a Certificate of Compliance in accordance with Secured by Design Homes Guide 2024 (or the relevant Secure by Design Guide(s) or an achieved Crime Prevention Standard) has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained.

Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates appropriate crime prevention measures and promotes a safe and secure environment for future residents.

No development shall take place until (other than site clearance) until a Piling Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Method Statement shall include:

o	Details of the type of piling to be undertaken; 
o	The methodology by which such piling will be carried out; 
o	Measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface water or sewerage infrastructure; and 
o	A programme for the works.

The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved Piling Method Statement.

Reason: To protect underground water and sewerage infrastructure and to prevent pollution of the water environment

The residential unit(s) hereby approved shall not be occupied until the development has been constructed or adapted to provide sufficient airborne and structure-borne sound insulation against externally generated noise and vibration. The insulation shall ensure that:

o	Internal noise levels do not exceed 35 dB LAeq,16hr (07:00-23:00) in bedrooms, living rooms, and dining rooms; 
o	Internal noise levels do not exceed 30 dB LAeq,8hr (23:00-07:00) in bedrooms; and 
o	Maximum noise levels (LAFmax) do not exceed 45 dB more than 10 times per night in bedrooms (23:00-07:00).
A scheme of mitigation measures, including provision for suitable alternative ventilation where internal noise levels would otherwise exceed the above thresholds with windows open, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the occupation of any unit. The approved scheme shall be implemented in full before occupation and shall take into account the Acoustics, Ventilation and Overheating (AVO) Guidance issued by the Association of Noise Consultants (ANC) and the Institute of Acoustics (IOA).

Reason: To protect the amenity of future occupiers from noise and disturbance, in accordance with relevant local and national planning policies.

No development other than works required for the laying of foundations shall commence until an acoustic report, written in line with the methodology in BS4142:2014+A1 2019, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from the mechanical plant and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the mechanical plant does not exceed a level of 5dB below the typical measured background noise level measured as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest or most noise affected residential property. 

Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/
 
Reasons: In the interests of good air quality and protecting public health

No dwelling hereby approved shall be occupied until a scheme for the implementation of waiting restrictions (double yellow lines) around the site access points have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The waiting restrictions shall be implemented in accordance with the approved scheme and retained thereafter. 

Reason: To ensure safe and unobstructed access to and from the development, in the interest of highway safety and to minimise potential conflicts between vehicles and pedestrians.

Prior to first occupation of the development, the 58 cycle parking spaces identified on drawings Proposed Ground Floor Plan Site A (0824-BPA-SA-00-DR-A-P1100 C) and Proposed Ground Floor Plan Site B (0824-BPA-SB-00-DR-A-P1110B) shall be provided on site.  
 
Reason: To ensure the development provides adequate on site cycle parking

a)	Prior to the commencement of the superstructure of the building,  typical details, including siting and design of plugs, of electric vehicular charging points including the design specification sheet to be provided in accordance with London Plan standards (minimum 20% of spaces to be provided with electric charging points and a further 20% passive provision for electric vehicles in the future) shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing.

b)	All electric charging points shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of the development approved and permanently maintained and retained.

Reason: To ensure that the development complies with the sustainable development policy requirements of the London Plan.

Notwithstanding the submitted SUDs strategy, prior to the commencement of development above ground, a final SUDS strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This shall be based on the strategy submitted but shall also identify:

o	Quality
o	On site A, RWPs should be directing discharge onto the surface of permeable paving instead of the subbase to avoid siltation and ease of inspection and maintenance.
o	On site B, RWPs should be directing discharge onto raingarden surfaces for the same reasons and overflow directed to the surface of permeable pavers before infiltrating.
o	Functionality
o	Cross sections, sizes and specifications of the proposed SuDS features must be provided in the context of the development accompanying drawings in Appendix G.
  
Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development

Prior to commencement (including demolition, ground works, vegetation clearance) of development, a construction environmental management plan (CEMP: Biodiversity) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The CEMP (Biodiversity) shall include the following:

a) Risk assessment of potentially damaging construction activities (including harm to otters).
b) Identification of "biodiversity protection zones".
c) Practical measures (both physical measures and sensitive working practices) to avoid or reduce impacts during construction (may be provided as a set of method statements).
d) The location and timing of sensitive works to avoid harm to biodiversity features.
e) The times during construction when specialist ecologists need to be present on site to oversee works.
f) Responsible persons and lines of communication.
g) The role and responsibilities on site of an ecological clerk of works (ECoW) or similarly competent person.
h) Use of protective fences, exclusion barriers and warning signs. 
i) No piles of debris or sharp materials should be stored within 30 m of the Turkey Brook's banks.
j)Any stored material near the Brook should be fenced off to avoid otters entering the area and using the stacks of materials as shelter.
k) No works should result in the illumination of the river corridor during the night. If night working is required, then lighting should be directional to prevent illumination of the river.
l) Any excavations within 30 m of the water's edge should be either covered, or ramps provided over night to allow suitable egress for otters or other mammals and ensure that they do not get trapped. 
m) Any open pipework with an outside diameter of greater than 150 mm must be covered at the end of each work day to prevent animals entering/becoming trapped.

The approved CEMP shall be adhered to and implemented throughout the construction period strictly in accordance with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.

Reason: To minimise impacts on biodiversity

Prior to the commencement of any construction activities on the site, a comprehensive Construction Logistics Management Plan (CLMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CLMP shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

1. Site Access and Egress:
   - Proposed routes for construction vehicles.
   - Measures to minimise traffic congestion and disruption.
   - Details of any temporary road closures or diversions.

2. Construction Traffic Management:
   - Management arrangements for construction traffic, including loading/unloading areas.
   - Delivery times to avoid peak traffic hours.
   - Measures to ensure pedestrian and cyclist safety.

3. Site Layout and Storage:
   - Site layout plan showing construction zones, storage, and welfare facilities.
   - Provisions for material and waste storage to reduce visual and environmental impact.
   - Mitigation measures for noise, dust, and other nuisances.

4. Construction Schedule:
   - Sequence and duration of construction phases.
   - Expected hours of work and vehicle movements per phase.

5. Health and Safety:
   - Compliance with health and safety regulations.
   - Risk mitigation for traffic and site hazards.
   - Wheel cleaning arrangements.
   - Use of operators committed to best practice (e.g., FORS membership or equivalent).

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved CLMP.

Reason:To ensure that construction works are managed in a way that minimises disruption to the local highway network, protects the amenity of neighbouring occupiers, ensures public safety, and promotes sustainable construction practices.

The development shall not commence until a Contamination Desk Study has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Desk Study shall include a Preliminary Risk Assessment comprising:

o	A review of all previous uses of the site; 
o	Identification of potential contaminants associated with those uses; 
o	A conceptual site model outlining potential sources, pathways, and receptors; and 
o	An assessment of any potentially unacceptable risks arising from contamination at the site.

No development shall take place until the Local Planning Authority has confirmed in writing that the submitted Desk Study is satisfactory.

Reason: To ensure that any contamination present on the site is properly identified and assessed, and to safeguard the health and safety of future occupants.

Having regard to Condition 17, should the approved Contamination Desk Study identify the need for further investigation, a Site Investigation Scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall provide sufficient information for a detailed assessment of the risks to all receptors that may be affected, including those off-site. The results of the site investigation shall be summarised in a generic or detailed Quantitative Risk Assessment, with conclusions and recommendations for any necessary actions.

Where the Risk Assessment identifies that remediation is necessary, the following shall also be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:

a) A Remedial Options Appraisal and/or Remediation Strategy detailing the proposed remediation and mitigation measures and how they will be implemented.
b) Where remediation is required:
i. A Verification Plan setting out the data to be collected to demonstrate that the remediation works have been completed to a satisfactory standard;
ii. A Monitoring and Maintenance Plan outlining provisions for long-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance, and contingency arrangements; and
iii. A Post-Completion Verification Report for each relevant phase of the development, including results of sampling and monitoring, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to occupation of that phase, demonstrating that the site meets the agreed remediation criteria.

Reason: To ensure that any contamination is properly identified, treated, and made safe, thereby safeguarding the health and safety of future occupants and users of the site.

If during the development contamination that has not previously been identified or unexpected contamination is found to be present then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out until the developer has submitted an updated addendum remediation strategy specifically for the previously unidentified contamination to the Local Planning Authority detailing how it shall be dealt with and obtained written approval from the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To ensure that any contamination is properly identified, treated, and made safe, thereby safeguarding the health and safety of future occupants and users of the site.

No development above slab level shall commence until a report detailing the external lighting scheme and how this will not adversely impact upon wildlife has been submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA. The report shall include the following figures and appendices:

o A layout plan with beam orientation
o A schedule of equipment
o Measures to avoid glare
o An isolux contour map showing light spillage to 1 lux.
The approved lighting plan shall thereafter be implemented as agreed.

Reason: To limit the impact of light pollution from artificial light on nature conservation

Prior to the commencement of the superstructure of the buildings, a scheme detailing measures to ensure the development achieves air quality neutral status, in accordance with the London Plan and relevant guidance, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include measures to minimise traffic-related emissions and other pollutant sources associated with the development. The approved measures shall be fully implemented prior to occupation and retained thereafter.

Reason: To minimise the impact of the development on local air quality and ensure compliance with the air quality neutral requirements.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the approved details and shall achieve an Urban Greening Factor (UGF) score of at least 0.4, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To ensure the development contributes to urban greening, biodiversity, and climate resilience

a)	Prior to the construction of the superstructure, the following details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

i.	Full details of biodiversity enhancements, to include plans showing locations and elevations of a minimum of one (1) bat brick, two (2) bird boxes and one (1) insect box to each building.

ii.            Ecological Management Plan in respect of the planting and biodiversity enhancement measures

b)           Prior to first occupation of the development, confirmation of installation of the biodiversity enhancements together with accompanying photographic evidence shall be submitted to and approved in writing, by the local planning authority.
 
The installation shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.

Reason: To enhance the site post development by providing suitable nesting features for birds, bats and invertebrates.

Compliance with Shadow Section 106 Agreement
No development shall take place on any part of the Site unless and until all parties with a (1) legal interest to the extent it may enable them to carry out any part of the development in the relevant part of the Site and (2) a legal locus to enter into a planning obligation pursuant to Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) have entered into such a planning obligation (unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority) in accordance with and substantially in the form of, the draft agreement appended to this decision notice ("Shadow S106").


Reason: The Council would have refused the planning application in the absence of the section 106 agreement and at the time of this permission being issued the applicant was not able to bind the legal interests in the development site under the section 106 agreement.  Development must not commence on any part of the Site until the legal interests that are capable of being bound under the section 106 agreement are so bound and the obligations are enforceable in accordance with the aims and objectives of policies Core Policies 38 and 46 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and to ensure all the terms of reference (on page 54-55 of the committee report) are met.

Compliance with S106 Obligations
No development shall take place on any part of the Site without fully complying with all the obligations, covenants, restrictions, terms and conditions (together "Obligations") in the Shadow S106, as if the party carrying out the development was a party to a planning obligation in the same form of the Shadow S106. Provided that this condition does not apply to any part of the site that the party has an interest in and that party has entered into a planning obligation pursuant to Condition 36.

Reason: For the avoidance of doubt of the full implementation of the planning permission.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.

Reason: To ensure the provision of adequate waste and recycling facilities in the interests of sustainability, public health, and residential amenity

Prior to the first occupation of the development, a Delivery and Servicing Plan (DSP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The DSP shall include details of the expected frequency and timing of deliveries and servicing activities, access arrangements, vehicle types, and measures to manage and minimise impacts on the local highway network. The approved plan shall be implemented upon first occupation and adhered to thereafter.

Reason: To ensure that delivery and servicing activities associated with the development are managed in a safe, efficient, and sustainable manner, minimising disruption to the local highway network, avoiding adverse impacts on highway safety, and protecting the amenity of neighbouring occupiers and land uses.

The development hereby permitted shall ensure that:

i. A minimum of 10% of the dwellings comply with Building Regulation Requirement M4(3) 'wheelchair user dwellings'; and
ii. All remaining dwellings comply with Building Regulation Requirement M4(2) 'accessible and adaptable dwellings'.

Evidence demonstrating compliance with these requirements shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority upon request.

Reason: To ensure that the development provides accessible and adaptable homes to meet the needs of all future residents, including wheelchair users.

Prior to first occupation of the development, the 3 disabled residential parking bay identified on drawing Proposed Ground Floor Plan Site A (0824-BPA-SA-00-DR-A-P1100 C) and 1 disabled residential parking bays identified on drawing Proposed Ground Floor Plan Site B (0824-BPA-SB-00-DR-A-P1110B) shall be provided on site. The spaces shall only be used for the parking of private motor vehicles for 'blue badge' residents and shall not be used for any other purpose. Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.
 
Reason: To ensure the development provides adequate on site car parking for disabled residents.
